text:
XXXX XXXX, the third-party company responsible for processing and disbursing student refunds on behalf of XXXX University , issued a direct deposit refund in the amount of approximately {$10000.00} on or around XXXX XXXX XXXX. According to the refund records, the funds were sent via ACH/direct deposit to Wells Fargo account ending in XXXX. 

However, the receiving Wells Fargo account had already been closed prior to the deposit attempt. Wells Fargos own mobile banking application clearly identifies the account as closed and unavailable for transactions. Despite this, the refund was still marked as issued, and there has been no clear explanation regarding whether the funds were rejected, returned, or are being held internally by the bank. 


XXXX XXXX advised me to contact Wells Fargo directly regarding the status of the funds and the return process. I contacted the bank seeking clarification and assistance regarding : Whether the ACH deposit was automatically rejected due to the account closure ; Whether the funds are being held internally despite the account no longer existing ; When the funds will be returned to XXXX XXXX so the refund can be reissued correctly ; and Why there has been a delay in rejecting or returning funds associated with a closed account.

Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq., and Regulation E, financial institutions are required to properly investigate and handle electronic fund transfer issues involving consumer accounts. Additionally, ACH transactions are governed by XXXX Operating Rules, which generally require that transactions sent to closed accounts be returned by the receiving financial institution within the required return timeframe rather than retained or delayed without explanation.

The Wells Fargo bank representative informed me that from the banks side the funds/account were essentially in limbo and stated there was nothing they could do other than tell me to wait. I was not provided any meaningful explanation, escalation, investigation details, ACH return information, or estimated timeline regarding the handling of the funds. Being told that over {$10000.00} in educational refund funds are in limbo without a clear answer as to whether the funds were rejected, internally held, or returned is unreasonable and has caused significant uncertainty, financial hardship, and distress.

Because Wells Fargo had prior knowledge that the account was closed and incapable of receiving deposits, the bank had a duty to promptly reject and return the ACH payment to the originating institution. Any unreasonable delay, internal hold, or failure to timely process the return may constitute improper handling of consumer funds and may interfere with my ability to access educational refund money intended for tuition, housing, transportation, and living expenses.

As a direct result of the banks actions and/or delay : I have been deprived access to over {$10000.00} in educational funds ; I have suffered financial hardship and uncertainty regarding the status of my money ; The originating institution has been unable to promptly reissue payment ; and I have spent significant time attempting to trace and resolve the transaction.

I am requesting : An immediate investigation into the status and location of the ACH funds ; Immediate return of the funds to XXXX XXXX if the account can not legally accept deposits ; Written confirmation regarding whether the ACH was rejected, returned, or internally held ; ACH trace and return information, including any applicable return codes ; Compensation or corrective action to the extent Wells Fargo failed to timely process the return in accordance with applicable banking and ACH rules ; and Assurance that Wells Fargo is complying with consumer protection laws governing electronic fund transfers and closed accounts.

Attached documentation includes : Screenshots from XXXX XXXX showing the refund issuance details and transaction information ; Screenshots from Wells Fargo confirming the receiving account ending in XXXX is closed.

The continued delay and lack of transparency regarding the handling of these funds has interfered with timely access to money intended for educational purposes and has caused avoidable financial distress.

Citi denied my dispute of a {$3600.00} unauthorized charge by XXXX XXXX without meaningfully addressing it under the applicable Truth in Lending Act, Fair Credit Billing Act, and Regulation Z standards, including the unauthorized-use standard and billing-error procedures. Citi instead applied a credit-card-fraud standard and concluded the charge could not be fraudulent because I had previously provided card information to the merchant for an earlier, authorized transaction ( see Ex. 1 and Ex. 2 ). That is not the correct test for unauthorized use. Citi continued to apply this incorrect framework in its XX/XX/XXXX response even after I expressly identified XXXX as the applicable standard in my XX/XX/XXXX letter ( Ex. 3 ) and my XX/XX/XXXX CFPB feedback in XXXX # XXXX. 

The most direct evidence that the XX/XX/XXXX charge was unauthorized is XXXX own contemporaneous billing conduct. Between XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX repeatedly demanded payment for the same {$3600.00}, including a XXXX XXXX billing statement marked PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT ( Ex. 10 ) and two emails with online payment links instructing us to Make an Online Payment ( Ex. 13 and Ex. 14 ). On XX/XX/XXXX, three days after the most recent pay online email, XXXX charged my card {$3600.00} without notification, without a receipt, and without my authorization. A merchant operating under standing card authorization does not send a PAST DUE notice and two pay online emails and then unilaterally charge the card three days later. I first sent Citi the PAST DUE statement as an attachment to an email sent XX/XX/XXXX ( Ex. 9 ; the PAST DUE statement is separately filed as Ex. 10 ) and sent it numerous times afterwards, including on XX/XX/XXXX ( Ex. 5 ), XX/XX/XXXX ( XXXX. XXXX ) and XX/XX/XXXX ( Ex. 6 ). The XX/XX/XXXX email included other XXXX emails from XXXX requesting payment. I also explained my unauthorized-use theory tied to them. Citi has never addressed this contradiction. 

Background This matter involves two XXXX XXXX charges of {$3600.00} each, billed to my Citi account on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX. The XX/XX/XXXX charge was authorized when I provided card information for the first installment in connection with the merchants written estimate ( Ex. 12 ). 

As of XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX itself acknowledged in writing that the final invoice amount was not settled. In an email from XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX ( Ex. 15 ), the merchant agreed to credit {$190.00} toward the final invoice ( {$99.00} for hotel reimbursement and {$100.00} for inconvenience ). Eleven days later, on XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX charged my card the full undiscounted {$3600.00}, without applying the credits it had agreed to and without my authorization. 

The XX/XX/XXXX charge was not authorized. I was not present when the charge was made, did not provide my card, did not authorize the charge by phone or in writing, and did not receive a receipt. I discovered the charge on XX/XX/XXXX, while reviewing my Citi account. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a single dispute covering both the unauthorized XX/XX/XXXX charge and XXXXXXXX XXXX defective work ( Citi assigned Case ID XXXX ). Because Citi 's online dispute form required me to select a single category, I selected goods/services not delivered as expected the sewer system was not working and that issue was foremost in my mind. I clarified in writing two days later that the XX/XX/XXXX charge was also unauthorized, in a XX/XX/XXXX email to XXXX ( XXXX. XXXX ). Regulation Zs billing-error procedures ( 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ) cover both unauthorized use and disputes involving goods/services, and my written notice cured any ambiguity well within the 60-day FCBA window. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, after additional defects in XXXX XXXX  work emerged, I filed a separate dispute as to the XX/XX/XXXX charge ( Citi assigned Case ID XXXX ). This CFPB complaint concerns only the first dispute, the XX/XX/XXXX unauthorized charge under Case ID XXXX. 

Scope of This Complaint My first CFPB complaint, Case # XXXX, was filed because Citi was not engaging substantively with my dispute. At that time, Citi had repeatedly requested documentation I had already submitted, was issuing inconsistent communications, and had not provided a written explanation of its determination. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, in feedback submitted through that case, I expressly narrowed my claim against Citi to the XX/XX/XXXX, charge of {$3600.00} only ( Ex. 24 ). My feedback stated : I am not asking Citi to reverse both charges through the billing dispute process. My primary claim against Citi is that the XX/XX/XXXX, charge was unauthorized under 15 U.S.C. 1643 and should be reversed ( {$3600.00} ), along with any interest or fees that accrued on the disputed balance and correction of any adverse credit reporting. I reserved all other claims against the merchant for defective workmanship, consequential damages, and unpaid credits, which I am pursuing through the North Carolina Attorney Generals Consumer Protection Division and the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX Contractors.

Citis XX/XX/XXXX response did not address the narrower claim I presented in the XX/XX/XXXX feedback. The XX/XX/XXXX letter continued to refer to two disputed charges from a plumbing merchant and relied in part on the argument that the total of the two charges also matched the total price on the merchants initial estimate. Citi was on notice of both the narrowed scope of my claim and the XXXX framework as of XX/XX/XXXX, and its XX/XX/XXXX response engaged with neither. This complaint concerns only Citis failure to properly investigate and its failure to respond to my unauthorized-use claim regarding the XX/XX/XXXX charge. 

Procedural History and Citis Repeated Documentation Requests The relevant procedural history is as follows : XX/XX/XXXX I filed the dispute the day I discovered the unauthorized charge. 

XX/XX/XXXX I emailed XXXX expressly stating that I did not authorize the second charge ( Ex. 7 ). 

XX/XX/XXXX I submitted Citis dispute form ( Form ID XXXX ) with a detailed dispute summary and timeline ( Ex. 8 ). The dispute summary listed Unauthorized Charge. XXXX charged my credit card on XX/XX/XXXX, without my authorization as Claim # 1, followed by additional numbered claims regarding workmanship. Paragraph I on page 7 further addresses the unauthorized credit charge, as does XXXX XXXX XXXX on the timeline. My submission included multiple attachments, including the XXXX Estimate ( Ex. 12 ), the XXXX Statement marked PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT dated XX/XX/XXXX ( Ex. 10 ), and the XX/XX/XXXX email from XXXX XXXX acknowledging the agreed credits ( Ex. 15 ). In response to Citis question on its form about how the charge was made, I wrote : Not in person or on phone. I do not know how they charged my card for the second payment. I had not authorized them to do so and did not give them my card. I did not receive a receipt. I only learned they charged my card when I noticed it on my Citi account. ( Ex. 8 ). 

XX/XX/XXXX I emailed Citi under dispute ID XXXX and expressly advised that much of the documentation I had submitted related to the other XXXX dispute XXXX XXXX. I wrote : If possible, could you please combine the files or review them together so the full context is clear? ( Ex. 16 ). This put Citi on notice that the two XXXX disputes involved overlapping facts, documents, and context. Citi did not substantively respond to that request. 

XX/XX/XXXX I emailed Citi clarifying that there was both defective service and a credit card charge that we did not approve, again stating that XXXX charged my credit card without authorization. 

XX/XX/XXXX Citi issued one letter stating that it was unable to identify or determine that a billing error occurred and reversing the conditional credits ( Ex. 21 ). Although Citis records may reflect that two letters were issued on this date, one for each of the two XXXX case IDs, I received only one such letter on or about XX/XX/XXXX, as evidenced by the screenshot of my Citi customer portal ( Ex. 19 ). This was for XXXX XXXX. 

XX/XX/XXXX I called Citi the day after I received the XX/XX/XXXX denial letter. The Citi representative on that call told me that Citis notes reflected that the merchant had never responded to Citis dispute submission. I again stated that I did not authorize the XX/XX/XXXX charge. Following that conversation, Citi reopened the investigation. 

XX/XX/XXXX / XX/XX/XXXX Citi sent two parallel Billing Dispute Update Important Information letters, one for each of the two XXXX XXXX case IDs ( XXXX for the XX/XX/XXXX charge and XXXX for the XX/XX/XXXX charge ) ( Ex. 18 ). The letters bore a XX/XX/XXXX date and demanded additional documentation by XX/XX/XXXX. Both letters stated that [ o ] nce this information is received, we will be happy to continue our investigation further. Citi also sent email requests dated XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX in a thread titled Citi Billing Dispute : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX  : {$3600.00}, {$3600.00} : XXXX ( Ex. 5 ). The email body likewise stated that Citi was investigating the amount of {$3600.00}, {$3600.00}, but the email listed only one reference number, XXXX. Although the letters were dated XX/XX/XXXX, they were not delivered through my portal until XX/XX/XXXX a seven-day delay confirmed by the portal screenshot, which shows a 'Date Sent ' of XX/XX/XXXX for both letters ( Ex. 19 ). The XX/XX/XXXX response deadline therefore gave me only seven days to respond, not the fourteen contemplated by the letters ' XX/XX/XXXX date. The timing is also notable in relation to Citi 's XX/XX/XXXX 'final denial ' : Citi dated the letters nine days after that denial and delivered them sixteen days after it, and Citi 's own XX/XX/XXXX letter confirms that the disputes were not formally reopened until XX/XX/XXXX three days after the letters reached me. 

XX/XX/XXXX I responded to Citis XX/XX/XXXX email request ( Ex. 5 ) with multiple attachments, including the XXXX Estimate ( Ex. 12 ), the XXXX Statement marked PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT ( Ex. 10 ), and other billing documents. In my response I wrote : I have two disputes related to the same amount. First, XXXX charged my card on XXXX [ XXXX ] without authorization. I again stated that the work was still disputed. Also on XX/XX/XXXX, I separately emailed Citis Legal Department ( XXXX XXXX ) and Executive Response Unit ( XXXX XXXX ) directly, copying the billing disputes team ( Ex. 17 ). In that email, I identified both dispute IDs ( XXXX and XXXX ) and explained that my initial XXXX dispute concerned an unauthorized charge, while a later XXXX dispute concerned the same merchant and defective services. I requested escalation to ensure that the dispute is being properly investigated and handled in accordance with applicable consumer protection laws. I again asked Citi to confirm ( 1 ) that the dispute remained open and under review, ( 2 ) the deadline for submitting additional materials, and ( 3 ) that I would receive a written explanation of the final determination. XX/XX/XXXX Citi reopened the disputes, as later confirmed in Citis XX/XX/XXXX letter ( Ex.2 ), which states that when the disputes were reopened on XX/XX/XXXX, the amounts were temporarily suspended. The same day, I emailed Citis Executive Response Unit and mentioned again that XXXX had charged my card on XX/XX/XXXX without authorization ( Ex. 20 ). I again asked three specific procedural questions : ( 1 ) whether Citi had all of the information I previously submitted regarding the billing disputes on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, ( 2 ) the deadline for submitting any additional materials, and ( 3 ) whether I would receive a written explanation of the final determination ( Ex. 20 ). My XX/XX/XXXX email noted : I have asked these questions regarding my billing dispute numerous times since XX/XX/XXXX and have yet to receive a response. Instead, I just get more requests asking me to send information that I have already submitted. Citi did not directly acknowledge or respond to my XX/XX/XXXX email, and the written determinations Citi eventually issued on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, did not address the procedural questions I had asked. 

XX/XX/XXXX I responded to Citis XX/XX/XXXX letter ( made available XX/XX/XXXX ) by the XX/XX/XXXX deadline with a written response and multiple attachments ( Ex. 22 ). My response opened by flagging the delivery timing : I am writing in response to your letter dated XX/XX/XXXX. Please note that although your letter is dated XX/XX/XXXX, I did not receive it until XX/XX/XXXX. I was given only seven days to respond, not the fourteen days contemplated by the letters XX/XX/XXXX date. My response expressly stated that ( 1 ) the services were not properly completed and the plumbing system failed shortly after the work was declared finished, and ( 2 ) the charge to my credit card on XX/XX/XXXX was made without my authorization while the work remained actively disputed. The attachments included the XXXX Estimate ( Ex. 12 ), the XXXX Statement marked PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT ( Ex. 10, marking the third submission of that document to Citi ), and the detailed dispute summary and timeline that listed Unauthorized Charge as Claim # 1 ( Ex. 8 ). XX/XX/XXXX Citis Billing Dispute team emailed me yet another set of documentation questions, stating : In response to your recent communication with us. We needed specific details to continue with our investigation to resolve the dispute in your favors ( Ex. 5, see also Ex. 6 ). This XX/XX/XXXX email was part of the same Citi-created email thread that listed both {$3600.00} XXXX charges in the subject line and body but included only one reference number, XXXX. I responded the same day with a detailed written argument and multiple attachments ( Ex. 6 ). My response expressly distinguished the first {$3600.00} charge, paid on XX/XX/XXXX, from the second {$3600.00} charge, made on XX/XX/XXXX. I wrote that the second charge was made even though I did not authorize this charge, nor did they send a receipt nor notify me that they were charging my card. I also explained : On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX sent a Past Due notice even though the system had not been inspected and the pipes were still exposed ; On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX sent my husband an email with a statement and invoice reflecting the XX/XX/XXXX payment ; and On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX again emailed my husband requesting payment of the remaining balance. My response also stated : I intentionally did not pay the remaining balance because the system was not functioning when XXXX claimed the job was complete. I expressly invoked the Fair Credit Billing Act, asking Citi to confirm that this dispute is being handled in accordance with applicable billing dispute requirements under the Fair Credit Billing Act, and confirm that I will receive a written determination. My XX/XX/XXXX attachments included XXXX Invoice # XXXX by name ( Ex. 11 ), the XX/XX/XXXX email from XXXX to my husband ( Ex. 13 ), the XX/XX/XXXX email from XXXX to my husband ( Ex. 14 ), and the XXXX Statement marked PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT ( Ex. 10 ). 

XX/XX/XXXX I submitted a complaint with CFPB ( XXXX ), seeking a clear status update, confirmation that Citi has all necessary documentation, and a written determination consistent with applicable billing dispute requirements ( Ex. 24 ). 

XX/XX/XXXX Citi issued a written determination ( Reference Number XXXX ) declining credit ( Ex. 2 ). The determination characterized the issue as XXXX of credit card fraud, concluded that the XX/XX/XXXX charge can not be considered fraudulently transacted because I had provided your account information to the merchant for billing purposes, stated that a copy of the actual invoice was not provided, and stated that the disputed amounts would now accrue interest. Citis statement that a copy of the actual invoice was not provided is factually incorrect : on XX/XX/XXXX, I provided XXXX Invoice # XXXX to Citi ( Ex. 11 ), the PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT Statement ( Ex. 10 ), and the emails to my husband with invoices attached ( Ex. 13 and Ex. 14 ). Citis XX/XX/XXXX determination did not address the XXXX Statement marked PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT ( Ex. 10 ), which I had submitted to Citi four separate times ( XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX ) and which is the single most direct evidence that the merchant did not have standing authorization to charge my card. 

Later the same day ( XX/XX/XXXX ), I sent Citi a written response identifying specific factual and legal errors in Citis determination and asking two direct questions : ( 1 ) whether Citi evaluated my unauthorized-use claim under 15 U.S.C. 1643 and what evidence supported its conclusion that the XX/XX/XXXX charge was authorized, and ( 2 ) whether Citi considered Sweetwaters XX/XX/XXXX PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT statement in evaluating authorization ( Ex. 3 ).

XX/XX/XXXX I submitted CFPB feedback in Case # XXXX narrowing my claim against Citi to the XX/XX/XXXX charge only and expressly identifying 15 U.S.C. 1643 as the applicable standard. ( Ex. 24 ). 

XX/XX/XXXX Citis Executive Response Unit acknowledged receipt of my XX/XX/XXXX letter ( my letter to Citi is Ex. 3 ), assigned Citi Reference Number XXXX, stated that my communication will receive a deliberate and thorough review, and stated that a response was anticipated within 15 calendar days ( Ex. 4 ). 

XX/XX/XXXX Citis Executive Response Team issued a letter ( Ex. 1 ) that did not answer either of my XX/XX/XXXX questions. The XX/XX/XXXX letter did not address XXXX, did not identify any evidence that I authorized the XX/XX/XXXX charge, did not address the PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT statement, did not address Sweetwaters XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX emails to my husband, did not address my XX/XX/XXXX written argument tying those documents to the unauthorized-use issue, did not acknowledge the narrowed scope of my claim, and did not engage with the substance of my XX/XX/XXXX correspondence or XX/XX/XXXX feedback. Instead, the letter referred to me internally as the cm, summarized Citis prior position, reiterated the credit-card-fraud framing, directed me to contact the merchant directly, and reaffirmed that the disputed amounts would now be subject to interest.

Why Citis Fraud Framing Does Not Answer the Authorization Issue Citis XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX letters analyze the XX/XX/XXXX charge under a credit-card-fraud standard and conclude that the charge can not be fraudulent because I had previously provided card information to the merchant. That is not the test. My claim is not that an unknown third party stole my card. My claim is that XXXX was not authorized to charge my card on XX/XX/XXXX. I made the applicable legal standard and the supporting facts explicit in writing on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. Citi nonetheless continued to apply the wrong framework. Providing card information for XXXX authorized transaction does not constitute authorization for all future charges. 

Sweetwaters own contemporaneous billing conduct demonstrates that XXXX was not acting under standing authorization. Citi had the XX/XX/XXXX PAST DUE statement in its possession from XX/XX/XXXX onward. Although the two XXXX disputes had separate reference numbers, I expressly asked Citi on XX/XX/XXXX to combine the files or review them together ( Ex. 16 ), and Citis own XXXX email thread treated the two disputes as related by listing both {$3600.00} charges. Citi had the XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX payment-link emails and my written explanation tying them to the unauthorized-use issue from XX/XX/XXXX onward : On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX sent a billing statement marked PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT for {$3600.00}, demanding that I remit payment ( Ex. 10 ). I submitted this statement to Citi on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX Plumbing emailed my husband a Statement and Invoice with the instruction See payment link here : Make an Online Payment ( Ex. 13 ). I submitted this email to Citi on XX/XX/XXXX. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, three days before the unauthorized charge, XXXX XXXX emailed my husband Invoice # XXXX with the subject line Your Invoice from XXXX XXXX, the statement The job is complete. Please find your invoice from XXXX XXXX  attached below! and the instruction Pay online at : Make an Online Payment ( Ex. 14 ). I submitted this email to Citi on XX/XX/XXXX. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, with no further communication, no receipt, and no notification, XXXX charged my card {$3600.00}. 

A merchant operating under standing card authorization does not send a Past Due Please Remit statement, then send the customer pay online payment-link emails twice in five days, and then unilaterally charge the card three days later without further communication. XXXX  own pre-charge conduct is incompatible with any claim of standing authorization. 

Citi has had all of these documents for months. The XXXX PAST DUE statement and the XX/XX/XXXX email from XXXX XXXX acknowledging the agreed credits were submitted on XX/XX/XXXX with my initial dispute packet ( Ex. 10 and Ex. 15 ). Citi resubmitted its request for documentation on XX/XX/XXXX, and I again provided the PAST DUE statement, the XXXX Estimate, and additional billing documents again on XX/XX/XXXX ( Ex. 5 ). On XX/XX/XXXX I provided additional attachments, including XXXX Invoice # XXXX by name and the XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX merchant emails sending payment links to my husband ( Ex. 6, Ex. 11, Ex. 13, and Ex. 14 ). I expressly identified the Past Due notice and the XX/XX/XXXX merchant email in writing in my XX/XX/XXXX response. Citis XX/XX/XXXX determination nevertheless stated that a copy of the actual invoice was not provided. That statement is factually incorrect. 

The XX/XX/XXXX authorization was a one-time phone authorization. Technician XXXX XXXX called XXXX office, and I provided card information over the phone to a XXXX finance representative for a single installment payment of {$3600.00}. I did not provide my card to XXXX again, did not authorize any recurring or standing charges, did not sign any authorization document, and did not authorize the XX/XX/XXXX charge in any form. Notably, XXXX own Invoice # XXXX ( Ex. 11 ), which Citi has had since XX/XX/XXXX, records the XX/XX/XXXX payment method as XXXX. The XX/XX/XXXX payment was in fact made on my Citi XXXX XXXX XXXX, the same account on which Citi posted the disputed XX/XX/XXXX charge. The merchant 's own records therefore misidentify the network of the card it claims to have on file ( which is a material inaccuracy that undercuts any inference that XXXX possessed reliable standing authorization ), and the merchant 's records identifying a XXXX  can not be the source of authorization on my XXXX account. 

Citi has had nearly five months to identify any signed authorization for the XX/XX/XXXX charge. It has not done so. Invoice # XXXX contains a pre-printed Customer Authorization block, but the signature lines on the copy in Citis possession are blank. Despite multiple submissions on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX, and despite my explicit written articulation of the unauthorized-use theory on XX/XX/XXXX, Citi has never identified any signed authorization, receipt, recorded authorization, merchant submission/representment materials, transaction authorization data, internal notes, or other documentation showing that I gave actual, implied, or apparent authority for the XX/XX/XXXX charge. If Citi or the merchant possesses a signed authorization, I request that it be produced. 

Citis Procedural Conduct Citis procedural conduct throughout this dispute is itself relevant to whether Citi conducted a reasonable investigation under 12 C.F.R. 1026.13 ( f ). Four patterns stand out : First, Citi compressed deadlines on the consumer while extending its own timelines. Citis XX/XX/XXXX letters set a XX/XX/XXXX deadline based on the date of the letters, but my Citi customer portal shows the letters were not made available to me until XX/XX/XXXX ( Ex. 19 ). That gave me seven days to respond, not the fourteen contemplated by the letters XX/XX/XXXX date. Citi gave itself approximately two months from its XX/XX/XXXX 'final denial ' ( and seven weeks from the formal reopen on XX/XX/XXXX ) to issue the XX/XX/XXXX determination. 

Second, Citis own communications blurred the two disputes. On XX/XX/XXXX, I asked Citi to combine the files or review them together because the two XXXX disputes involved overlapping documentation ( Ex. 16 ). Citi did not substantively respond. Then, on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, Citi sent email requests in a thread identifying both {$3600.00} charges but only one dispute reference number, XXXX ( Ex. 5 ). I responded in that Citi-created thread. Citi later issued determinations on both disputes at the same time. Citi can not reasonably disregard the substance of my XX/XX/XXXX response merely because its own email thread listed only one of the two dispute numbers.

Third, Citi sent two parallel we require additional documentation letters dated XX/XX/XXXX ( delivered through the portal XX/XX/XXXX ), one for each case ID, both requesting overlapping documentation that I had already submitted on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX after Citis purported final denial and before Citi formally reopened the investigation on XX/XX/XXXX. Citi has not explained how the disputes could be both resolved and the subject of active documentation requests at the same time.

Fourth, Citi did not answer specific procedural questions I asked in writing on multiple occasions. My XX/XX/XXXX email to Citis Legal Department and Executive Response Unit ( Ex. 17 ), my XX/XX/XXXX email to the Executive Response Unit ( Ex. 20 ), and my XX/XX/XXXX response to Citis documentation request ( Ex. 22 ) each asked Citi to confirm whether previously submitted materials had been received, the deadline for additional submissions, and whether I would receive a written explanation of the final determination. My XX/XX/XXXX letter ( Ex. 3 ) additionally asked Citi to confirm whether it had evaluated the XX/XX/XXXX charge under XXXX and what evidence it relied on. Citi did not directly acknowledge or answer any of these procedural questions. Citi eventually issued written determinations on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX addressing the underlying dispute, but those determinations did not answer the specific procedural questions or identify the regulatory standard Citi applied. 

New Conduct Since the Closure of CFPB Case # XXXX Three pieces of new conduct since the prior CFPB case warrant attention : First, Citis XX/XX/XXXX letter ( Ex. 1 ) followed Citis XX/XX/XXXX commitment to a deliberate and thorough review of my XX/XX/XXXX letter ( Ex. 4 ), but it did not engage with the specific questions I posed, did not acknowledge the narrowed scope of my claim as expressed in my XX/XX/XXXX CFPB feedback ( Ex. 24 ), and did not address XXXX even though I had expressly identified it as the applicable standard. The letter did not address the PAST DUE PLEASE REMIT statement, did not address the invoice, did not address the XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX merchant pay online emails, did not address my XX/XX/XXXX written articulation of the unauthorized-use theory, and did not acknowledge the substance of my XX/XX/XXXX correspondence. It summarized Citis prior position, without addressing any of the specific points raised in my XX/XX/XXXX letter or XX/XX/XXXX feedback. This indicates that the response did not reflect the deliberate and thorough review Citi had promised. 

Second, Citis XX/XX/XXXX letter stated that, with the investigation complete, the disputed amounts would be included in the Balance Subject to Interest Charge, and Citis XX/XX/XXXX letter reaffirmed that interest would now accrue. I object to interest being assessed on the XX/XX/XXXX charge while Citi has not meaningfully addressed my claim under the applicable TILA, FCBA, and Regulation Z standards, including whether the charge was authorized and what evidence supports Citis determination. Citi acknowledges in its XX/XX/XXXX letter that the disputed amounts were properly excluded from interest accrual during the pendency of the dispute. An investigation that does not satisfy the reasonable-investigation requirements of 1026.13 ( f ), and that applied a credit-card-fraud standard rather than the unauthorized-use or billing-error standards required by 1026.13 ( a ) and 1643, does not entitle Citi to resume interest assessment on amounts that remain in dispute under 1026.13 ( g ).

Third, Citis reversal of the conditional credits on XX/XX/XXXX and its decision to treat the disputed {$3600.00} as a valid balance has had a measurable adverse effect on my credit. My XXXX  score declined from XXXX in XX/XX/XXXX to XXXX in XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX, which is a XXXXpoint drop ( Ex. 23 ). The decline tracks Citi 's XX/XX/XXXX reversal of the conditional credits, which inflated my reported credit utilization on the Citi account at a time when the underlying authorization question remained unresolved and the disputed {$3600.00} should not have been treated as a valid balance under 1666a. 

Until Citi evaluates the XX/XX/XXXX charge under the correct legal standard and produces evidence supporting any conclusion of authorization, the disputed {$3600.00} should not be reported as a valid balance, should not accrue interest, and should not be treated as a settled item on my account.

This CFPB complaint is also a formal request for debt validation to Mid-South Adjustment , Co., Inc under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and a dispute of the accuracy and completeness of the account under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ).

Subject : Consumer Complaint Regarding Citibank Credit Card, Account Access Failure, Lack of Billing Transparency, and Credit Reporting Risk Monday, XX/XX/year> To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint regarding Citibanks handling of the transition of my XXXX XXXX credit card account from XXXX to Citibank. Citibanks servicing failures have left me unable to access my account, review my statement, verify transactions, confirm whether my card or statement was properly delivered, or make an informed payment before my upcoming due date. 

I contacted Citibank on XX/XX/XXXX in attempt to gain access to their online portal for the first time since my account was switched from XXXX to Citibank. Upon connecting with a representative, I was informed that my payment was due in two days. If I had not called, I would not have known about the due date as a statement was not mailed to my home and I did not receive an electronic notification The representative was unable to provide access Citibanks online system and I still have not been provided with a timely alternative means of reviewing my statement or transaction history. I do not know whether the replacement card was lost in the mail, whether my statement was properly delivered, or whether there are any unauthorized or fraudulent charges on the account.

When I contacted Citibank, I was told that the bank could accept a payment over the phone, but representatives would not provide the transaction information necessary for me to verify what I would be paying. I was also told that it would take approximately seven days to receive a statement, despite the fact that my payment deadline was imminent.

This creates a serious consumer-protection concern. Citibank is effectively placing me in the position of either paying an unverified balance blindly or risking late fees, adverse credit reporting, and harm to my credit score because Citibank has failed to provide timely access to basic account information.

I am particularly concerned that Citibank may assess late fees or report negative payment information to credit bureaus despite the fact that any payment delay would be caused by Citibanks own transition, account-access, and servicing failures. A consumer should not face financial penalty or credit harm because a bank can not provide timely access to statements, transaction information, or account-management tools.

This issue also raises concerns about fraud prevention and consumer account security. Because I can not access my account or review recent transactions, I can not determine whether unauthorized charges have occurred. Citibank has not provided an adequate process for me to verify the balance before payment, nor has it provided meaningful support to resolve the access issue before the due date. 

The transition from XXXX to Citibank appears to have been poorly executed from a consumer-servicing standpoint. Customers should not be transferred into a system where they can not access their accounts, can not review statements, can not verify transactions, and may still be subject to late fees or credit consequences. This reflects a failure to manage a major account transition in a manner that protects consumers.

I am requesting that regulators review Citibanks handling of this transition and its customer-servicing practices, including whether affected customers are being exposed to late fees, adverse credit reporting, fraud risk, or other harm due to lack of timely account access and billing transparency.

I am also requesting that Citibank be required to confirm that no late fees, interest charges, or adverse credit reporting will result from its failure to provide timely access to my account information and statement.

This matter is not simply an inconvenience. It is a basic failure of account servicing, billing transparency, and consumer protection during a credit card transition. A national banking institution should not expect consumers to make payments without access to the information necessary to verify the amount owed, while simultaneously exposing those consumers to potential fees and credit consequences. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX
label: Credit card

This complaint is filed jointly by the primary borrower and the co-signer of an Ally Financial auto loan dated XX/XX/XXXX. The loan was for approximately {$34000.00} financed at 13.94 percent APR for 84 months at {$650.00} per month, secured by a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

Allys system then performed repeated internal Reallocations that spread the cancellation refund across future scheduled payments instead of treating it as a one-time principal reduction.

The result was that Ally generated and delivered seven consecutive monthly billing statements ( XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX ) showing Amount Due : {$0.00} and Statement Total : {$0.00}. Voluntary payments were made during this period because the borrowers knew the loan still existed.

As of late XX/XX/XXXX, the Ally app showed an outstanding balance of {$30000.00} while the credit bureaus were reporting {$31000.00}, a {$1500.00} discrepancy between Allys own records on the same date. text:
I am filing a second complaint against Citibank regarding a personal loan application that was formally approved and, after XXXX days of not being able to accept it due to an internal system failure, they let it expire. Now, I reapplied using exactly the same information that resulted in the previous approval, and Citi has denied my application. 

For context : Citibank approved my loan application and confirmed that, in their system, the loan was pending acceptance, and the credit line showed as available ( XXXX ). However, when I attempted to log in and accept the loan terms, their platform consistently fails and does not allow me to proceed, asking me to call them. This issue is entirely on Citibanks side and prevents me from accessing an already approved financial product. 

Over the past 22 days, I have contacted Citibank XXXX times through their customer service channels and personal bankers. Despite these repeated efforts : No representative has been able to resolve the issue. 
I have not received any meaningful update or estimated timeline. 
The only response I consistently receive is that I must wait for the Tech Department to fix the issue, '' since " it is clearly a Technical Issue on our side. '' They got extremely rude asking me to stop calling and wait XXXX hours for a representative to call me ( which has not happened ). 

This response is not acceptable. Citibank has failed to provide a functional mechanism to accept the loan, yet continued to treat the application as time-sensitive and finally it let it expire. 

Compounding the issue, Citibank conducted a hard inquiry on my credit report as part of the application process. I was informed that if I do not accept the loan within 21 days, they will require a new application and an additional hard credit inquiry. This of course has negatively impact my credit scoredespite the fact that I was absolutely unable to accept the loan, and no Citibank employee could fix the issue, solely due to Citibanks internal system malfunction. 

This situation creates an unfair and unreasonable outcome : 1. I had an approved loan that I can not access.

2. I faced credit harm due to circumstances entirely outside my control.

3. Citibank did not provid a workaround, escalation path, or resolution timeline.

4. Citibank let the approval expired.

5. Now Citibank has conducted a new credit inquiry and has rejected my new loan application, which had exactly the same information as the application that was previously approved.

This matter reflects a breakdown in Citibanks digital onboarding process and a complete failure to protect consumers from avoidable credit harm. 

After XXXX weeks and a first complaint filed, Citibank replied on XX/XX/year>. Frankly, Citis response was deeply unsatisfactory and fails to address the actual substance of my complaint. Rather than engaging with the factual background I provided, Citi issued a generic and conclusory response that ignores the operational reality I have been dealing with for nearly four weeks. At no point did I claim that my loan application was denied. The issue is precisely the opposite : Citi approved the loan, but I had repeatedly been unable to complete the acceptance process because Citis own system fails during the electronic bank account verification stage. This has occurred consistently and repeatedly despite numerous attempts over approximately 24 days. Several Citi employees have also tried to complete the loan application on the phone and in person in a New York branch, and the same error appeared. Most concerning, Citi now states in its CFPB response that it confirmed that there were no system errors or issues on Citibanks end. Throughout this process, Citi agents repeatedly acknowledged that the issue appeared to be technical in nature, that the application was stuck in the system, and that they were escalating the matter to technical support because they themselves could not resolve it. If, as Citi now claims, there was never any system issue, then I request that Citi explain : ( 1 ) why multiple representatives stated that the matter had to be escalated to technical support ; ( 2 ) why no representative was ever able to complete the electronic acceptance process despite repeated attempts ; ( 3 ) why I was repeatedly instructed to wait for the tech team ; ( 4 ) why the issue was unresolved after more than three weeks later ; and ( 5 ) why Citibank has now denied my new loan application under the exact same information they approved XXXX XXXX weeks ago. 

Citis response also entirely disregards the central concern raised in my complaint : that I was exposed to the risk of expiration of an approved loan offer, and now to a second hard credit inquiry, because Citis process was not functioning properly in practice regardless of whether Citi now labels it a system error.

Moreover, Citis proposed solution namely, requiring me after weeks of failed attempts to abandon the electronic process and instead complete a paper-check workaround only further demonstrates that Citi was unable to make the approved electronic acceptance process function properly. The CFPB should note that Citis response does not meaningfully address the repeated failed attempts, the contradictory information provided by Citi representatives, the lack of any effective escalation path, the substantial amount of time spent attempting to resolve an issue that Citi now broadly dismisses without explanation ; and the recent denial of the new application under the same circumstances I had been approved XXXX weeks ago. 

At this stage, Citis response appeared clearly designed to formally close the complaint without genuinely addressing the operational failure that gave rise to it.

My dispute specifically demanded strict proof of ownership, chain of title, merger documentation tying the specific account to any alleged XXXX XXXXXXXX transfer, complete balance accounting, original contractual documentation, proof of authority to collect in Texas, proof of the required Texas surety bond under Texas Finance Code 392.101, complete transactional history, date of first delinquency information, and competent business records sufficient to establish the alleged debt.

However, the company failed to provide the documentation requested. The response did not contain account-level merger documentation, did not establish chain of title, did not provide a complete itemized accounting, did not provide proof of Texas surety bond compliance, did not provide competent business records establishing ownership or standing, and did not provide the complete records necessary to validate the alleged balance.

Instead, the company primarily sent generic cover letters and credit card statements, which do not constitute competent validation of ownership, balance accuracy, legal standing, or authority to collect. 

On XX/XX/year>, I mailed a formal rejection of deficient validation and notice of continued noncompliance to Rausch Sturm LLP by certified mail. XXXX tracking confirms delivery on XX/XX/year>, at XXXXXXXX XXXX

text:
To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this response regarding Shellpoint Mortgage Servicings XX/XX/XXXX, response to my CFPB complaint concerning my mortgage loan, Trial Period Plan, and loan modification review. 

While I appreciate Shellpoints acknowledgment that service and system issues affected my ability to submit my XX/XX/XXXX trial payment, I respectfully dispute several of the companys conclusions and request an additional review and investigation. 

First, I want to make clear that I have consistently acted in good faith and have always intended to keep my home and continue making affordable mortgage payments. 

Shellpoints response confirms : * Their online payment portal reflected additional fees that prevented submission of the required trial payment amount. 
* I mailed a payment in good faith during the servicing transfer period. 
* The payment was returned after being sent to the prior servicer. 
* I immediately contacted Shellpoint seeking alternative payment options. 
* The final trial payment was ultimately accepted, and * The trial modification was not canceled due to the payment submission issues. 

However, the primary issue remains unresolved. 

When I entered the Trial Period Plan in XX/XX/XXXX, I reasonably believed that successful completion of the trial payments would result in an affordable and sustainable permanent mortgage payment close to my prior payment amount of approximately {$3400.00}. 

I was instructed to make : * an initial payment of {$500.00} ; and * three trial payments of {$7200.00}.

During conversations with Shellpoint representatives, including representative XXXX XXXX, I was never clearly informed that the permanently modified mortgage payment would become approximately {$7100.00} per month. 

The first written documentation clearly stating a permanent payment of {$7100.00} appears in the XX/XX/XXXX, modification package. Prior to that time, Shellpoints Trial Period Plan documents repeatedly described the modification as a path toward more affordable mortgage payments and more manageable terms.

The Trial Period Plan documents also stated : Any difference between the amount of the trial period payments and your regular mortgage payments should not significantly change the amount of your modified mortgage payment.

A permanent payment of {$7100.00} was more than twice my original mortgage payment and was not affordable, manageable, or sustainable given my financial circumstances.

Additionally, Shellpoints own online servicing portal continued to display : * Monthly Payment : {$3400.00} ; and * Starting XX/XX/XXXX, your new payment will be {$3500.00}. 

This directly contradicts the separate modification documents, which state that my payment would be {$7100.00} effective XX/XX/XXXX. 

These conflicting and inconsistent payment disclosures created substantial confusion and reinforced my understanding that my permanent modified payment would remain near my prior affordable payment level. 

I also respectfully dispute the characterization that I voluntarily canceled the loan modification. 

I did not reject mortgage assistance or refuse to keep my home. Rather, after reviewing the proposed permanent terms, I informed Shellpoint that : * The payment was unaffordable. 
* My income had changed due to job loss and reduced earnings. 
* I wanted to provide updated financial documentation. 
* I wanted a new, affordable loan modification review based on my current income, and * I wanted to continue making affordable monthly payments while a review was pending. 

I specifically informed Shellpoint that I had lost my previous job and later secured new employment at a lower income level. 

I attempted to provide updated financial information and supporting documentation reflecting my current financial circumstances. However, Shellpoint representatives informed me that updated financial documents were not needed because they already had all our information on file. 

Further, when I later attempted to pursue a new modification review, I was unable to properly submit a new loan modification application and updated financial documentation because I was effectively prevented or blocked from submitting a new review request. 

I can afford payments approximately equal to my prior monthly mortgage payment of {$3400.00}, but I can not afford a payment over {$7000.00} per month. A modification that more than doubles my monthly payment is neither sustainable, affordable, or realistic given my current income and financial circumstances.

I continue to request : 1. A full reevaluation for an affordable loan modification using my CURRENT income and financial documentation ; 2. Written clarification regarding the conflicting payment amounts reflected in Shellpoints online portal and modification documents ; 3. Copies of all : * call recordings; * servicing notes; * underwriting calculations; * affordability analyses; * investor restrictions; * and internal records regarding my modification review ; 4. Written confirmation that I may continue making affordable monthly payments while the loss mitigation review is pending ; 5. Confirmation that foreclosure activity will remain paused while this dispute and modification review remain unresolved.

I respectfully request that CFPB continue reviewing this matter, including the inconsistent payment disclosures, the affordability determination process, the denial of meaningful reconsideration, and the inability to submit a new modification application using updated financial information. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX XXXX Phone : XXXX Email : XXXX XXXX

text:
On XXXX XXXX XXXX, Capital Management Services , LP ( CMS ) mailed an initial collection letter regarding an alleged XXXX account with a claimed balance of {$7900.00}. The letter offered a 27 % settlement totaling {$2100.00} and instructed me to make payments directly through CMS. The letter identified XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX as both the original creditor and current creditor. 

On XXXX XXXX XXXX, within the statutory validation period, I mailed a formal written dispute and debt validation demand to CMS via Certified Mail No. XXXX. USPS tracking confirms the dispute packet was delivered to CMS on XXXX XXXX XXXX  at XXXX XXXX in XXXX, XXXX XXXX 

My dispute specifically invoked the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ) ) and Texas Finance Code 392.202. I formally disputed the alleged debt in its entirety and demanded that CMS cease all collection activity until proper validation was provided.

In my written dispute, I specifically requested the following documentation and disclosures : 1. The name and physical mailing address of the original creditor.

2. A complete itemized accounting of the alleged {$7900.00} balance.

3. A copy of the original signed contract or agreement.

4. The date of last payment and the date of first delinquency.

5. Documentation establishing CMSs authority to collect on behalf of XXXX. 

6. Texas surety bond information pursuant to Texas Finance Code 392.101.

7. Proof that CMS was authorized to conduct collection activity within the State of Texas.

8. The final billing statement issued prior to charge-off.

9. Documentation verifying that I was the correct consumer beyond name and address matching.

10. Written confirmation of the applicable statute of limitations and calculation date.

11. Written confirmation of any intent to report to consumer reporting agencies.

I also specifically requested written confirmation regarding : whether the alleged debt had been sold, assigned, or securitized whether any Form 1099-C had been issued whether the balance reflected prior accounting write-offs or adjustments My dispute additionally directed CMS to cease all telephone communications and stated that all communications must occur in writing only.

Despite receipt of my timely dispute, CMS failed to provide the requested validation documentation. 

Instead, on XXXX XXXX XXXX, CMS mailed a response containing only limited account statements, a generic cover letter, and a copy of a card agreement. The response failed to provide critical information specifically requested in my dispute. 

CMS failed to provide : Texas surety bond information required under Texas Finance Code 392.101 proof of authority to collect in Texas documentation establishing legal authority to collect on behalf of XXXX a complete itemized accounting of the alleged balance documentation reconciling the charged-off balance with the amount being collected documentation regarding securitization or assignment status any information regarding Form 1099-C reporting competent business records establishing ownership and authority documentation identifying how the balance evolved after charge-off proof establishing that the alleged debt remained legally enforceable The XXXX XXXX XXXX response instead instructed me to contact CMS to discuss  payment arrangements and settlement options despite the unresolved validation deficiencies. 

After receiving my timely dispute and without curing the validation defects, CMS continued collection activity. 

On XXXX XXXX XXXX CMS mailed another settlement solicitation letter offering installment payment arrangements regarding the same disputed debt. The XXXX XXXX letter again attempted to induce payment while the debt remained disputed and unresolved.

The XXXX XXXX XXXX  collection letter was sent after CMS had already received my dispute and after CMS failed to provide the specific validation materials requested in my XXXX XXXX XXXX dispute letter. 

I believe CMS violated the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, including 15 U.S.C. 1692g ( b ), by continuing collection activity after receiving my timely written dispute without first providing competent validation of the alleged debt. 

I also believe CMS violated 15 U.S.C. 1692e and Texas Finance Code 392.304 by attempting to collect and represent the balance as valid while failing to provide requested documentation substantiating the amount being collected and their authority to collect the debt in Texas.

Additionally, CMS failed to provide the Texas surety bond information specifically requested under Texas Finance Code 392.101, yet continued collection activity and payment solicitation efforts anyway.

The responses mailed by CMS did not demonstrate that a meaningful investigation had been conducted. Instead, CMS continued sending settlement solicitations while material portions of the validation request remained unanswered. 

I am requesting that the CFPB formally investigate CMSs collection conduct, continued collection activity after dispute, failure to provide competent validation, failure to provide requested Texas compliance documentation, and attempts to collect an alleged debt that remains disputed and insufficiently validated.

text:
XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, IL XXXX Wenesday, XX/XX/year> To Whom It May Concern : RE : Complaint Regarding Automated Credit Card Payment Holds Following Verified ACH Withdrawal of Funds I am submitting this complaint regarding potentially unfair and inconsistent payment-hold practices involving large electronic credit-card payments withdrawn from verified consumer bank accounts but not promptly restored to available credit. 
Attached as supporting documentation is a mini-statement from my financial institution, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, reflecting the underlying account activity associated with these transactions. 

The attached records show : loan advances deposited into my established checking account, successful ACH withdrawals by the credit-card issuers, and the corresponding transfer activity during the relevant time period. 

During the same general timeframe, I made several substantial electronic payments from the same long-established checking account that I have successfully used for years. 

One payment of approximately {$8000.00} made toward a Visa Signature account with an {$11000.00} credit limit was processed normally and the corresponding available credit was restored the following business day. However, substantially similar payments involving : approximately {$4000.00} to the XXXX XXXX XXXX associated with XXXX XXXX ; and approximately {$5000.00} to Citibank were subjected to extended payment holds despite the funds already having been withdrawn from my bank account. 
In both cases : the ACH payments were successfully initiated, the funds were removed from my checking account, the payments originated from a long-established verified bank account, and there were no fraud alerts reported by my financial institution. 

I contacted my bank directly and was informed that no fraud flags or suspicious activity indicators existed on my account in connection with these transactions. 
I subsequently contacted both credit-card issuers multiple times and escalated the matter to supervisory personnel. During those conversations, I was informed that the transactions had been automatically flagged because of the payment amounts involved and that the restrictions were system generated. 
When I requested a specific explanation regarding : what factual basis triggered the alleged fraud concern, what particular risk indicators were identified, and whether any meaningful human review had occurred, I did not receive a clear or substantive explanation beyond generalized references to automated system controls. 

I further offered to provide direct proof from my bank confirming successful ACH settlement and availability of funds. I also offered to transfer additional funds to further secure the account balances. I was informed that additional payments would likely be subjected to the same automated restrictions. 

This raises significant concerns regarding : the transparency of these automated payment-hold systems, the absence of meaningful manual review, and the possibility that legitimate consumer payments are being broadly restricted through opaque algorithmic processes despite confirmed withdrawal and settlement of funds. 

The inconsistency in treatment is particularly concerning. 

If one institution can restore approximately {$8000.00} in available credit the following business day using the same banking relationship and substantially similar payment conditions, it is unclear why other institutions require approximately one week to restore available credit after the funds have already been removed from the consumers account. 
These delays create tangible financial consequences for consumers. 

By withholding available credit after taking possession of the funds, issuers may : artificially elevate consumer credit-utilization ratios, reduce available borrowing capacity, delay purchases and transactions, place accounts into unnecessary liquidity constraints, and potentially contribute to adverse credit-reporting consequences if elevated balances are reported during the hold period. 
In my case, approximately {$1800.00} in pending XXXX purchases involving project materials, including bolts, nuts, rivets, and related hardware, were placed on hold due to the restricted availability of credit despite the fact that payment funds had already been withdrawn from my bank account. 

This issue also raises broader public-interest concerns. 

Public financial data indicates that : approximately 208 million Americans hold at least one credit card ; total U.S. credit-card debt exceeds approximately {$1.00} trillion ; the average revolving balance among indebted cardholders is approximately {$7800.00} ; and many American households maintain relatively limited liquid savings reserves. 
Under these conditions, temporary restriction of thousands of dollars in available credit after confirmed payment withdrawal may create substantial financial hardship for consumers. 
Additionally, even temporary institutional control over large aggregate volumes of consumer funds may create meaningful float value during the holding period. For example : if 1 million consumers experienced an average temporary hold of {$5000.00} for seven d
ays, at a hypothetical 4.5 % annualized rate, the aggregate temporary float value could exceed several million dollars during that short period alone. 

I am not alleging intentional misconduct without evidence. However, the practices described above appear opaque, inconsistently applied, heavily automated, and potentially harmful to consumers who have already surrendered verified funds. 
Accordingly, I respectfully request : A written explanation regarding why substantially similar ACH payments received materially different availability treatment ; Confirmation regarding the date and time the ACH transfers were considered settled and verified by each institution ; Clarification regarding whether delayed restoration of available credit may impact utilization reporting to credit bureaus ; Disclosure regarding whether supervisory personnel possess authority to override automated payment holds after ACH settlement has been confirmed ; Clarification regarding the specific criteria used to trigger these payment restrictions ; Regulatory review into whether such automated payment-hold practices unfairly restrict consumer access to credit after payment funds have already been collected. 

Consumers should not lose access to thousands of dollars in available credit after verified funds have already been withdrawn from established accounts merely because an unexplained automated system flagged the transaction. 
Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

text:
I am submitting this complaint against Ability Recovery Services regarding the reporting of an allegedly delinquent medical collection account that is inaccurate, incomplete, and not properly verified under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act ( FDCPA ) and the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 

The company is reporting a derogatory collection account on my consumer credit reports in the amount of {$2400.00}, allegedly associated with XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. This account is being furnished to consumer reporting agencies despite the absence of competent documentary evidence establishing its accuracy, completeness, or my legal liability. 

The information being reported is materially deficient and fails to meet federal standards because it does not include : Itemized billing statements supporting the alleged balance ; Dates of service or treatment ; Explanation of Benefits ( EOB ) or insurance payment history ; Documentation showing how the {$2400.00} balance was calculated ; Signed agreement or financial responsibility documentation establishing liability ; Proof of assignment or legal authority to collect the alleged debt ; Date of first delinquency necessary for accurate credit reporting ; Any documented method of verification used to furnish this account. 

Pursuant to 15 U.S.C. 1692g, a debt collector must provide validation of a debt upon dispute. I dispute the validity, accuracy, and enforceability of this alleged obligation. To date, Ability Recovery Services has failed to provide competent verification sufficient to establish that the debt is accurate or legally owed.

Furthermore, under 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), consumer reporting agencies and furnishers are required to maintain reasonable procedures to assure the maximum possible accuracy of information reported. Furnishing a medical collection account without complete underlying documentation, including insurance adjudication records and itemized billing, does not satisfy the standard of maximum possible accuracy. 

Medical debt reporting is particularly susceptible to error due to insurance adjustments, coding discrepancies, duplicate billing, and administrative misallocations. In this case, the furnisher appears to be relying on conclusory account data rather than verifiable documentary evidence demonstrating that the alleged balance is correct and attributable to me. 

Under 15 U.S.C. 1692c, continued collection activityincluding credit reportingwithout proper validation following a dispute raises additional compliance concerns, particularly where the debt has not been substantiated with competent evidence.

Accordingly, I am requesting that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau require Ability Recovery Services and all associated consumer reporting agencies to : Conduct a reasonable investigation into this account consistent with FCRA requirements ; Provide complete documentary validation of the alleged debt, including itemized billing and insurance records ; Produce the full method of verification used to report this account ; Demonstrate proof of legal authority to collect and furnish this debt ; Cease furnishing any information that can not be fully verified ; and Permanently delete this account from all consumer reporting agencies if full and competent verification can not be produced. 

I also request preservation of all records, audit trails, internal notes, communications, and furnishing data used in connection with this account, including any automated matching or database verification processes. 
This complaint concerns violations and/or potential violations of : 15 U.S.C. 1692g 15 U.S.C. 1692c 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) All applicable provisions of the FDCPA and FCRA governing accuracy, validation, and reasonable investigation standards.

I request a formal written response supported by documentary evidence establishing the accuracy and legality of this reporting, or immediate deletion of the account from my consumer credit reports.

From XX/XX/XXXX through late XXXX, I maintained a flawless mortgage payment history through automatic draft payments with my prior servicer, XXXX XXXX XXXX. 

In late XXXX, servicing of my mortgage was transferred from XXXX to LoanCare/Lakeview. During this transition, automatic payments did not continue seamlessly, and I was required to establish a completely new online account and payment system. Because mortgage fraud and servicing scams are common, I did not immediately provide sensitive financial information until I verified the legitimacy of the transfer through multiple parties, including communications with XXXX, XXXX, LoanCare, and consultation with legal counsel. 

As a result of this servicing transition disruption, several payments in early XXXX were reported late to the credit bureaus. Once the transfer was verified and the new account established, I immediately resumed automatic payments and have maintained a perfect payment history for nearly three years since the incident. Prior to the transfer, I also maintained over two years of perfect payment history.

I submitted both a goodwill request and a formal Notice of Error under RESPA ( 12 CFR 1024.35 ). LoanCare responded by stating only that the payments were accurately reported and that notices of transfer had been mailed. However, LoanCare failed to meaningfully investigate or address the core issue I raised : whether the servicing transfer process itself caused the delinquency reporting through disruption of payment continuity and inadequate servicing transition procedures. 

My complaint is not simply about whether payments were technically reported late. My complaint is that the reported delinquency resulted directly from servicing-transfer disruption and breakdown of automatic payment continuity during the transfer process, despite my otherwise long-standing history of responsible mortgage payment behavior.

text:
What happened : I am a Citibank customer and my account currently has a fraud lock on it that Citibank has refused to resolve.

The underlying problem is that the phone number on file for my account contains a typo and is not a number I can receive calls or texts at. The number Citibank currently has on file is XXXX. The correct number is XXXX. These two numbers differ by a single digit transposition, which makes it self-evident that this is a typo and not a fraudulent attempt to change contact information to an attacker-controlled number.

When I attempted to correct this through a secure message in the Citibank mobile app, Citibank responded by placing a fraud lock on my account.

Today, I made multiple attempts to resolve this by phone. I was hung up on twice after long holds. On a third call, I finally reached a representative who required me to answer a series of identity verification questions, which I did successfully. After answering those questions, the representative told me there was no path forward and that they could not help me, because Citibank 's identity verification procedure requires confirming a code sent to the phone number on file which is the number containing the typo that I am trying to correct. When I requested to be transferred to a supervisor, the representative indicated he would transfer me, then hung up on me instead.

This creates an impossible loop : I can not update my phone number through the app ( the app message is what caused the fraud lock ), and I can not update it by phone ( because Citibank insists on verifying through the incorrect phone number, even after I successfully answered other identity verification questions, and because my request for supervisor escalation resulted in being disconnected ). In-person resolution is also not reasonably available to me. Citibank has no retail branch presence in XXXX, where I live only ATMs, which can not perform identity verification or account servicing. The nearest full-service Citibank branch is over an hour away from my home.

Compounding the harm, I am currently working against a time-limited promotional spending requirement on my account. Reaching this spending threshold within the promotional window is contingent on having access to my account. I have attempted to ask Citibank whether they will extend the deadline or waive the requirement given that their own fraud lock is preventing me from using my account, but Citibank representatives have refused to discuss, confirm, or answer any question about the spending requirement or anything else about my account until they confirm my identity, which they have already told me they can not do. As a result, I am at risk of losing the value of the promotional offer through no fault of my own, solely because of Citibank 's refusal to use any identity verification method other than the phone number that contains their typo.

I am effectively locked out of my own account, a Citibank representative has explicitly told me there is no path forward, my request for supervisor escalation was met with a hang-up, and Citibank 's inaction is causing me direct financial harm on a deadline.
label: Credit card

I am filing this formal complaint against Bank of America regarding an unauthorized and non-transparent interest charge of {$63.00} applied to my account on XX/XX/year>. Despite paying my previous statement balance in full before the due date, I was penalized with interest fees that were not clearly disclosed in my cardholder agreement.

This practice contradicts the standard industry expectation of a " Grace Period ''. Per Bank of America 's own general terms, interest is typically not charged on purchases if the entire balance is paid by the due date.

I believe the bank failed to provide clear and conspicuous disclosure that a " secondary '' interest trigger exists for purchases made immediately following a full balance payment but before the cycle close. I request a full refund of the {$63.00} fee and ask that the CFPB urge Bank of America to update their cardholder disclosures to prevent other consumers from being similarly misled.

Complaint Against Debt Collector Regarding Refusal to Honor Written Settlement Offer I am filing this complaint regarding a debt collectors refusal to honor the written terms of a settlement offer that was provided directly to me.

I received a written settlement communication from the company that contained language offering a settlement based on 20 % of the balance. The wording was clear and unambiguous as written. After reviewing the offer, I relied upon the exact language contained in the document in evaluating and responding to the proposed settlement terms.

After I attempted to proceed based on the written language of the offer, the company informed me that the phrase 20 % of was supposedly intended to read 20 % off and claimed the language was merely a typographical error.

The company is now refusing to honor the terms exactly as they were presented in the written settlement correspondence.

My concern is not merely that an error may have occurred, but that the company expects consumers to disregard or reinterpret official written settlement communications after the fact. Consumers should be able to reasonably rely on the plain language contained in formal collection and settlement notices without later being told the terms were different than what was actually written.

As the drafting party, the debt collector bears responsibility for ensuring that its settlement communications are accurate before being transmitted to consumers. In my view, refusing to honor the written language after it has been issued creates a misleading and unfair situation for consumers attempting to resolve debts in good faith.

I requested that the company provide : A copy of the original settlement offer ; A detailed explanation of the alleged typographical error ; The date the error was discovered ; Documentation showing whether corrected notices were issued to other consumers ; and Confirmation that no adverse credit reporting or collection activity would occur while this dispute remains unresolved.

To date, the company has refused to honor the settlement language as written.

I am requesting that the CFPB review this matter for potentially misleading or unfair debt collection and settlement practices and assist in ensuring that the company honors the written settlement terms provided.

Attached documentation includes copies of the settlement correspondence and related communications regarding the dispute.

I am submitting this complaint against Citibank , N.A . / Citi XXXX XXXX regarding unfair and misleading payment allocation practices involving deferred-interest promotional balances on my My Best Buy Credit Card account.

My account contained two separate deferred-interest promotional balances : 1. An 18-month deferred-interest promotional balance scheduled to expire on XX/XX/XXXX ; and 2. A 24-month deferred-interest promotional balance scheduled to expire on XX/XX/XXXX. 

The statement closing XX/XX/XXXX showed : * {$190.00} remaining on the XX/XX/XXXX expiring promotional balance ; * {$300.00} remaining on the XX/XX/XXXX promotional balance. 

Before the XX/XX/XXXX expiration date, I made sufficient payments specifically intended to satisfy the expiring promotional balance and avoid retroactive deferred-interest charges. 

The XX/XX/XXXX statement reflects : * XX/XX/XXXX XXXX payment of {$99.00} ; * XX/XX/XXXX online payment of {$160.00}. 

Total payments made before expiration : {$260.00}. 

This amount exceeded the remaining {$190.00} balance associated with the XX/XX/XXXX expiring promotional balance. 

Despite this, Citi allocated only {$29.00} toward the expiring promotional balance and instead applied approximately {$230.00} toward the separate promotional balance expiring in XX/XX/XXXX. As a direct result, Citi charged {$260.00} in retroactive deferred interest on XX/XX/XXXX. 

The core issue is that Citis online payment system does not provide consumers with a clear, transparent, or meaningful way to direct payments toward a specific promotional balance. The system simply allows consumers to make a payment without adequately warning that payments may be allocated in a way that triggers retroactive deferred-interest charges.

This payment-allocation structure is misleading and creates substantial consumer harm because consumers reasonably expect that payments made before a promotional expiration date will first satisfy the balance closest to expiration. Instead, Citis system allocated my payments in a manner that caused avoidable deferred-interest charges despite timely payments being made.

I believe these practices are unfair and potentially deceptive because : * consumers can not reasonably control or verify how payments will be allocated among promotional balances ; * the payment interface lacks sufficient transparency regarding allocation consequences; * consumers are exposed to large retroactive interest charges despite making timely payments ; * Citi financially benefits from the resulting deferred-interest charges.

Under Regulation Z and 12 C.F.R. 1026.53, deferred-interest promotional balances nearing expiration receive special payment-allocation protections intended to prevent consumers from being trapped by retroactive interest charges.

I contacted Citi customer service and spent approximately two hours attempting to resolve this issue. I escalated the matter through multiple representatives, supervisors, and a manager identified as XXXX. Citi representatives stated they could not reverse the charges because more than 60 days had passed and because their system allegedly could not process the correction.

The issue was not caused by a missed payment or delinquency. I made sufficient timely payments before the promotional expiration date. The harm resulted from Citis payment-allocation conduct and system design.
